title: Configuration before action
summary: Infrastructure as code means describing resources in files. Terraform reads those files and compares the desired result with recorded state.
introduction: Infrastructure as code means describing resources in files. Terraform reads those files and compares the desired result with recorded state. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Infrastructure as code means describing resources in files. Terraform reads those files and compares the desired result with recorded state.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Use a new local folder and Terraform 1.4 or newer for the built-in terraform_data examples. Read first. Do not add cloud credentials or run apply against an unknown project.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Terraform. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.
This prints the local Terraform version. It does not create any infrastructure.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain the difference between reading a plan and applying it.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A tool that can manage infrastructure must be pointed at the intended project.
For more detail later, use this [Terraform further reading](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/tutorials).
